newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - April 8.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.
- Hanbo Group founder Chung Tae-soo admitted giving money to three senior politicians other than the four lawmakers already indicted over the Hanbo loans scandal.
- State prosecutors said the three senior politicians Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo accused of taking money would initially be summoned for questioning.
- A government official said North Korea proposed for a meeting with U.S. and South Korean officials on April 16.
- Supreme court is set to rule on appeals virdicts for former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo on April 17.
- South Korea openly welcomed for the first time North Korea's bid to join the Asian Developement Bank as the starving Stalinist state appeared to be warming to proposed peace talks.
- North Korea has agreed in principle to a South Korean proposal for the establishment of a trade office to support southern business seeking to invest in the North.
